title: Pan-seared steak with garlic butter
summary: A restaurant-style steak with a proper crust: the best test of 'too hot or not hot enough'.
source: Written for REMY by Claude, timers from cook-times.json (2.5cm, medium-rare). Checked by Matthew on 2026-11-07.
equipment: Heavy frying pan (cast iron is best)
notes: Timers assume a steak about 2.5cm thick, cooked medium-rare. Remy should ask how thick it is and how they like it, and change the timers using the cook-times table (2cm / 2.5cm / 4cm × rare / medium-rare / medium / well done).
ingredients: 1 sirloin, ribeye or rump steak, about 2.5cm thick, out of the fridge for 20–30 minutes
1 tbsp oil with a high smoke point (vegetable or rapeseed)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 garlic clove, crushed with the side of a knife

steps.instruction: Pat the steak really dry with kitchen paper, then season it generously with salt and pepper on both sides. Tell Remy how thick it is and how you like it cooked.
looks_right: dry surface with no shine of moisture
salt and pepper visible on both sides
looks_wrong: wet steak straight from the packet (it'll steam, not sear)
raw meat juices touching other food, or the same board used for salad
steps.done_when: The steak is dry and seasoned, and Remy knows the thickness and doneness.

steps.instruction: Put the heavy pan on high heat for a few minutes until it's very hot, then add the oil.
looks_wrong: oil lying still with no shimmer (not hot enough yet)
steps.done_when: The oil shimmers and ripples when the pan is tilted.

steps.instruction: Lay the steak in the pan, away from you so the oil doesn't spit at you. Don't touch it, let the crust form.
looks_right: a loud sizzle the moment it goes in
looks_wrong: steak being poked, pressed or moved around (no crust)
steps.done_when: The first side has a deep brown crust (lift a corner with tongs to check).

steps.instruction: Flip the steak. Turn the heat down to medium, then add the butter, garlic and herbs. Tilt the pan and keep spooning the foaming butter over the steak.
looks_right: deep, even brown crust on the cooked side
butter foaming and turning nutty brown
looks_wrong: grey, pale cooked side (pan wasn't hot enough)
butter turning black (turn the heat down)
steps.done_when: Both sides are seared. A thermometer in the thickest part reads about 54–55°C for medium-rare (it rises to ~57°C while resting). For other doneness, use the food-safety table.

steps.instruction: Move the steak to a board and let it rest. Spoon the garlic butter from the pan over the top.
looks_right: steak resting untouched on the board
looks_wrong: cutting into it straight away (the juices run out)

steps.instruction: Slice against the grain (across the lines in the meat) into strips, and show Remy the inside.
looks_right: an evenly cooked inside (pink all the way through for medium-rare)
steps.done_when: Sliced and plated. Remy can comment on the colour, but must not call it 'safe' from looks; that's what the thermometer is for.
